newsitem.title: UK: Diana pulls out of landmine meeting at parliament.
newsitem.headline: Diana pulls out of landmine meeting at parliament.

text.p: Princess Diana has withdrawn from a controversial meeting at Britain's parliament on Wednesday with campaigners for an international ban on landmines, political sources said on Wednesday.

"We've been told that the princess won't be attending now," said an aide to one of the members of parliament who had invited Diana, ex-wife of heir to the throne Prince Charles, to meet the all-party Landmines Eradication Group.
Princess Diana's office had no immediate comment on whether or not she would attend.
Campaigners for a ban on landmines hailed her agreement to visit the House of Commons as a major boost.

But it ran into a storm of criticism from members of the main opposition Conservative party who said she risked contravening an unwritten rule that members of the royal family must not intervene in political issues.
Last month the new Labour government promised to destroy all Britain's anti-personnel mines by 2005, pursuing its pledge to put human rights at the centre of foreign policy.
In doing so, it adopted a tougher policy than the previous Conservative government of John Major.
The MP's aide said Diana would still meet the organisers of the group at a later date -- but presumably not at the House of Commons.
Diana, who toured war-ravaged Angola in January to meet landmine victims, has criticised countries which trade in landmines and has called for a worldwide ban.
